## Energy conservation of the two-stream equations and the conservative limit (`RadiationBand` albedo clamp) {#sec-ch02-conservation}

### Summary

A layer that only scatters must pass its net flux through unchanged, and a layer that absorbs must lose exactly
what it absorbs. Both statements follow from the two-stream equations for every closure of @sec-ch02-closures. The
closed-form solution that the Toon solver evaluates is a different matter: it is singular when the single-scattering
albedo is exactly 1. pyharp avoids that point by capping the albedo in `RadiationBand` before any solver runs; the
Toon kernels themselves do not.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Energy balance of @eq-ch02-closures-ode, @eq-ch02-conservation-divergence; the $\omega = 1$ limit.

**Data.** Per layer: $\gamma_1$ to $\gamma_4$, $\omega$; fluxes in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$.

**Placement.** Clamp in `RadiationBandImpl::forward`, before the solver call.

**Activation.** On in `RadiationBand` whenever the band's properties carry an albedo (`nprop > 1`); absent in the bare
Toon kernels.

**Guarantee / limits.** Conservation is exact; the closed form is singular at $\omega = 1$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $F_{\mathrm{net}}$, net upward flux including the direct beam [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $J$, mean
intensity [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$]; $B$, Planck function of the layer, linear in $\tau$
[$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$]; $k_1$, $k_2$, amplitudes of the homogeneous solution [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $C^{\pm}$,
particular solutions [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $R$, reflectance of a layer [-]; $\delta\omega$, albedo margin [-].

The clamp (@eq-ch02-conservation-clamp) is on in every `RadiationBand` call whose properties carry a single-scattering
albedo, that is, when some opacity returns more than the extinction (`if (nprop > 1)`); a direct call of the Toon
module skips it. Toon et al. prescribe the same remedy, with $1 - \omega$ ten times the machine
precision.[^ch02-conservation-tn]

### Derivation
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-divergence check_ch02_closures.py [C22] -->

**Step 1: divergence of the net flux.** Let $F_{\mathrm{net}} = F^{+} - F^{-} - \mu_0F_0e^{-\tau/\mu_0}$, where the
last term is the direct beam, positive downward. Subtracting the two lines of @eq-ch02-closures-ode and adding
$\mathrm{d}(\mu_0F_0e^{-\tau/\mu_0})/\mathrm{d}\tau = -F_0e^{-\tau/\mu_0}$ gives Toon's eq. (28),

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}F_{\mathrm{net}}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} = (\gamma_1 - \gamma_2)\left(F^{+} + F^{-}\right)
  + \left[1 - \omega(\gamma_3 + \gamma_4)\right]F_0\,e^{-\tau/\mu_0} .
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-divergence}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-divergence check_ch02_conservation.py [C1] -->

**Step 2: the conservative layer.** At $\omega = 1$ every closure has $\gamma_1 = \gamma_2$ (Meador-Weaver eq. 23),
and $\gamma_3 + \gamma_4 = 1$ (their eq. 21; `check_ch02_closures.py` sums the derived $\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_4$ of
each closure, as tagged for Appendix B). Both terms of @eq-ch02-conservation-divergence vanish: $F_{\mathrm{net}}$ is
constant through a conservative layer.

**Step 3: absorption.** Every closure of @sec-ch02-closures has $\gamma_1 - \gamma_2 = (1-\omega)/\mu_1$ with $\mu_1$
independent of $\omega$: $\mu_1 = \tfrac12$ for Eddington and the hemispheric mean, $3^{-1/2}$ for quadrature and
$\mu_0$ for the delta function. With Toon's mean intensity
$J = (F^{+}+F^{-})/(4\pi\mu_1) + F_0e^{-\tau/\mu_0}/(4\pi)$ (his eqs. 17, 18), @eq-ch02-conservation-divergence becomes

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}F_{\mathrm{net}}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} = 4\pi(1-\omega)\,J ,
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-absorption}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-absorption check_ch02_conservation.py [C3] -->

the power absorbed per unit optical depth. In the thermal form the beam terms are replaced by the sources
$\mp 2\pi(1-\omega)B$ (Toon eq. 15), there is no direct beam, and the same steps give
$4\pi(1-\omega)(J - B)$: absorption minus emission.

**Step 4: the closed form.** In a homogeneous layer the general solution of @eq-ch02-closures-ode is Toon's eqs.
(19) and (20),

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{+}(\tau) &= k_1 e^{\lambda\tau} + \Gamma k_2 e^{-\lambda\tau} + C^{+}(\tau) , \\
F^{-}(\tau) &= \Gamma k_1 e^{\lambda\tau} + k_2 e^{-\lambda\tau} + C^{-}(\tau) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-closed}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-closed check_ch02_conservation.py [C17] -->

with $\lambda$ and $\Gamma$ of @eq-ch02-closures-hm-a and the particular solutions $C^{\pm}$ of Toon's eqs. (23),
(24) and (27). @eq-ch02-conservation-closed is evaluated as `xk1`, `xk2`, `gam`, `Ep`, `Em`, `Cp` and `Cm` in
`toon_mckay89_shortwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}).

**Step 5: why it fails at $\omega = 1$.** There $\gamma_1 = \gamma_2$, so $\lambda = 0$ and $\Gamma = 1$. Both
homogeneous terms of @eq-ch02-conservation-closed become $(k_1 + k_2)(1, 1)$: the determinant of the basis,
$1 - \Gamma^2$, is zero, and the basis carries no net diffuse flux. The solution it has lost is linear in $\tau$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{+} - F^{-} &= c , \\
F^{+} + F^{-} &= 2\gamma_1 c\,\tau + d ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-linear}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-linear check_ch02_conservation.py [C8] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch02-conservation-linear the solution the closed form lacks at omega = 1, not evaluated by pyharp -->

for constants $c$ and $d$, which solves @eq-ch02-closures-ode with $\gamma_1 = \gamma_2$ and no source. Toon et al.
state that eqs. (19)-(20) do not apply at $\omega$ exactly 1 (p. 16,290). The tridiagonal matrix the shortwave kernel
assembles from @eq-ch02-conservation-closed inherits the singularity. Near $\omega = 1$, $\lambda$ vanishes like
$(1-\omega)^{1/2}$: $\lambda \approx [3(1-\omega)(1-g)]^{1/2}$ for quadrature and $2[(1-\omega)(1-g)]^{1/2}$ for the
hemispheric mean.

**Step 6: the conservative answer.** For one conservative layer of optical thickness $\Delta\tau$ over a black
surface, Meador and Weaver's eq. (24) gives the reflectance in closed form,

$$
R = \frac{\gamma_1\Delta\tau + (\gamma_3 - \gamma_1\mu_0)\left(1 - e^{-\Delta\tau/\mu_0}\right)}{1 + \gamma_1\Delta\tau} ,
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-r1}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-r1 check_ch02_conservation.py [C12] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch02-conservation-r1 reference solution, not evaluated by pyharp -->

with transmittance $1 - R$. The closed form of @eq-ch02-conservation-closed tends to @eq-ch02-conservation-r1 as
$\omega \to 1$; the error falls like $1 - \omega$.

**Step 7: the clamp.** `RadiationBandImpl::forward` replaces the albedo by

$$
\omega \leftarrow \min\left(\omega,\ 1 - \delta\omega\right) ,
$$ {#eq-ch02-conservation-clamp}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-clamp check_ch02_clamp_pyharp.py [C1] -->
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-conservation-clamp check_ch02_clamp_pyharp.py [C2] -->

with $\delta\omega = 10^{-12}$ for double and $10^{-6}$ for other types. @eq-ch02-conservation-clamp is computed as
`ssa_margin` in `RadiationBandImpl::forward`
({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}}). It trades an error of order
$\delta\omega$ for a solvable system. Check `[C1]` of `check_ch02_clamp_pyharp.py` runs a `RadiationBand` with the
Toon solver and an opacity that returns $\omega = 1$: the solver input holds $1 - 10^{-12}$ bitwise and the band's
fluxes equal those of the Toon module called with $1 - 10^{-12}$; in single precision the input holds
$\mathrm{float32}(1 - 10^{-6})$ (`[C2]`).[^ch02-clamp-run]

**What is exact.** Steps 1 to 3 are exact identities of the two-stream equations for every closure, and Step 6 is
exact for the conservative two-stream problem. The clamp is the one approximation. The checks are
`derivation-checks/check_ch02_conservation.py` and `derivation-checks/check_ch02_closures.py`.

### Numerical method

The Toon kernels join the layers of @eq-ch02-conservation-closed through a tridiagonal system, described in the
chapter on Toon's method. Check `[C9]` reads the two-layer shortwave rows and right-hand side from the kernel source,
confirms that they equal its own transcription entry by entry, and confirms that their solution is that of the
conditions they encode (the downward flux at the top, continuity of $F^{+}$ and $F^{-}$ at the interface, the surface
reflection) at two rational points. At $\Gamma = 1$ that matrix has determinant zero for every $e^{\lambda\Delta\tau}$
and surface albedo, and so does the system of those conditions: the singularity comes from the closed-form basis of
@eq-ch02-conservation-closed, not from the assembly. The shortwave scaling maps $\omega = 1$ to exactly 1 in double
precision, so $\gamma_1^2 - \gamma_2^2$ is round-off of either sign, and $\lambda$ comes out not a number, 0 or below
$10^{-7}$ depending on $g$ (check `[C10]`, a numpy transcription; the split is compiler dependent and not quoted).

At 53-bit precision, for one layer ($\Delta\tau = 1$, $g = 0.75$, $\mu_0 = 0.5$, black surface), the error of the
closed-form $R$ against @eq-ch02-conservation-r1 is smallest at $1 - \omega = 10^{-12}$, about $2\times10^{-12}$. It
grows to about $5\times10^{-9}$ at $10^{-8}$ (truncation) and $7\times10^{-10}$ at $10^{-16}$ (cancellation; check
`[C14]`). The double-precision margin is at the optimum for this case.[^ch02-conservation-run] The figure of this
scheme is not provided: its module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| albedo clamp | {{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}} | `ssa_margin` | `nprop > 1` |
| shortwave closed form | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}} | `lam`, `gam`, `xk1`, `xk2` | always |
| longwave closed form | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}} | `alp`, `lam`, `gam` | `planck` |

: Code map of the conservative limit. {#tbl-ch02-conservation-code}

1. `RadiationBandImpl::forward` ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandImpl::forward repo=pyharp >}})
   converts attenuation to optical thickness and then, if `prop` has an albedo channel (`nprop > 1`), caps channel
   `ISS` with `clamp_max_(1.0 - ssa_margin)`.
2. `toon_mckay89_shortwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}})
   has no path for $\omega = 1$; its guard `g2 = 1e-10` acts at $\omega = 0$.
3. `toon_mckay89_longwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}})
   gets `alp` $= 0$ and `gam` $= 1$ at $\omega = 1$.

: Tests of the conservation identities. {#tbl-ch02-conservation-tests}

All 19 claims of the conservation check and the 3 of the clamp check pass.[^ch02-conservation-run][^ch02-clamp-run] No
pyharp test runs a Toon solve at or near $\omega = 1$; the clamp check runs the compiled path there.
(`DeviceTest.shortwave_resonance_is_continuous` covers $\lambda\mu_0 = 1$.)

### Limits

- CANDIDATE, from checks `[C9]` and `[C10]` and measured by `[C3]` of `check_ch02_clamp_pyharp.py`: a direct call of
  the Toon module, which skips the clamp, with $\omega$ exactly 1 in a layer, solves a singular system, so its fluxes
  are set by round-off: their values depend on the order of floating-point operations and are not quoted here.
  The check asserts only that they differ, by more than $10^{-6}\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ in the band and at all in
  the bare kernels, from the fluxes at the nearest albedos below 1. For one layer of $\Delta\tau = 1$, $g = 0.5$,
  albedo 0.2, the shortwave $F^{+}$ at the top is $0.2183742$ at $\omega = 1 - 10^{-12}$ ($\mu_0 = 0.5$,
  $F_0 = 1$) and the longwave one $275.5325\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ (level temperatures 300 and 250 K); at
  $\omega = 1$ the same layer gives other values[^ch02-clamp-run]. A solver comparison that calls the Toon module
  directly at $\omega = 1$ gets fluxes of no physical meaning.
- The single-precision margin $10^{-6}$ was not compared with the closed form here.
- The clamp changes only $\omega$; a conservative layer then absorbs a fraction of order $\delta\omega\,\Delta\tau$,
  which is not measured.

[^ch02-conservation-tn]: Source: Toon et al. [@reading02] p. 16,291, citing W. J. Wiscombe, "The delta-Eddington
    approximation for a vertically inhomogeneous atmosphere", NCAR Technical Note TN-121+STR, 1977. That note has no
    DOI on Crossref or DataCite and was not read; it is not Wiscombe's delta-M paper [@reading05].
